description: Overstretched or slightly torn shoulder muscles, usually from overuse or a sudden load.
Irritated rotator cuff tendons; pain when lifting the arm sideways or overhead.
Overloaded tendons on the outer elbow; pain when gripping or extending the wrist.
Stretched wrist ligaments, often after a fall on the hand; pain when bearing weight on it.
Strained neck muscles; stiffness and pain when turning or tilting the head.
Strained lower back muscles; pain when bending, lifting or twisting.
Strained inner thigh muscles; pain when bringing the legs together or changing direction.
Strained muscles at the back of the thigh; pain when bending the knee or sprinting.
Non-acute pain around the kneecap; worse when squatting, kneeling or using stairs.
Overloaded tendon below the kneecap; pain when jumping, squatting or landing.
Pain along the inner shin bone from repeated impact, common in running and jumping.
Strained calf muscles; pain when pushing off, rising on the toes or running.
Overloaded tendon above the heel; stiffness in the morning and pain when pushing off.
Stretched ankle ligaments, usually from rolling the foot inward; swelling and pain when walking.
Broken bone confirmed or suspected; the affected area must not be loaded until a doctor allows it.
Joint forced out of position, usually the shoulder or a finger; needs medical care before any training.
